(ii) w=6 is the maximal unit count among imaginary quadratic fields, achieved uniquely by K — verified via the embedding argument: ζ_n∈ a quadratic imaginary field requires φ(n)≤2, i.e. n∈{1,2,3,4,6}; n=3,6 both give K (w=6), n=4 gives the DIFFERENT field ℚ(i) (w=4), every other field has w=2.
missing_rows.why_missed: Every a–j row states a value belonging to K taken alone; none asks how that value ranks against the same invariant computed over K's peer class (all imaginary quadratic fields). This is a different logical type of claim (comparative/classification, not internal), and a method built by sampling 'K's own invariants, one type at a time' has no slot that ever produces it. Flagged verbatim in B1067's census: 'the two textbook extremality facts are absent as facts.'

missing_rows.definition: g1/g2/g3 test finite-order characters (ray/Dirichlet characters mod 2^k), and j4 tests chi_{-3} -- all torsion-valued, all reachable by varying a finite conductor. K's CM theory (the j7 curve, j-invariant 0) carries a structurally different object: the algebraic Hecke character psi: A_K^x/K^x -> C^x of nontrivial infinity type (weight 1, z |-> z on the archimedean component), whose L-function L(psi,s) is the curve's Hasse-Weil L-function and whose values on principal ideles are algebraic-integer GENERATORS in O_K, not roots of unity. This is genuinely infinite order and requires the ONE archimedean place of K explicitly -- data no finite-conductor row can carry. Whether psi's torsion restriction (or its ell-adic avatar) reconnects to mu_3/mu_6 the way B1042's abelianization characters did is untested.
missing_rows.why_missed: The g/j series is organized by finite modulus (2,4,8) or a single named finite-order character (chi_{-3}); every item in that family is torsion-valued. A Hecke character of nontrivial infinity type is not a member of that family at ANY modulus -- it needs the archimedean place, which none of a1-j7 touch (only finite places 2,3,4,8 and residue primes 2,3,5,7,13 appear). A modulus-indexed generation method has no natural index that reaches the archimedean component, so it structurally cannot produce this row.

critics.notes: Method: read WORKING_RULES.md (binding) and the pattern row's own source (frontier/B1042_trit_morphism/{b1042_cells.py,FINDINGS.md,arc_verdict.json}); read B266 and B727's FINDINGS to check the deflation rule against them; then reconstructed 2T's character table exactly (Fraction/Q(omega) arithmetic, no numerics) and computed a genuinely new diagram automorphism not in B1042, verifying it in-sandbox rather than asserting it (script: (scratchpad)). Separately, B1041's and B1042's own sealed text both name an explicit fence ('the FMT's S3... untouched') pointing at live, repo-acknowledged missing territory; I ran the actual discriminant factorization (sympy) to determine what that S3's resolvent field actually is, rather than assuming it was Q(sqrt(-3)) -- it is Q(sqrt(77)), a clean negative that redirects (not confirms) the natural guess toward the casus-irreducibilis/Kummer-base role instead. I checked and rejected one plausible-looking candidate before finalizing: the compositum 2T⊂2I (index 5, tetrahedral-in-icosahedral) as a bridge to Q(sqrt5), which B727's own banked finding ('2O forces sqrt2, 2I forces sqrt5 -- both real quadratic; {E6} is the only exceptional McKay label reachable over an imaginary-quadratic field') already covers thoroughly enough that a fresh row there would likely be B727-in-costume. Confidence ranking: crit4-0 highest (fully computed, verified in-sandbox, mechanistically forced); crit4-1 high (the negative half is computed/verified, the positive Kummer-base connection is a documented repo fact newly linked to this specific chain, not yet itself computed as a descent test); crit4-2 moderate (a genuine categorical gap -- no infinity-type/archimedean-place row exists anywhere in the enumeration -- but I have not run a computation tying it back to the 2T/McKay side, so its descent-relevance is asserted more loosely than the other two). "conductor" in crit4-1/crit4-2 refers to the ray-class/Hecke-character modulus (the corpus's other "conductor" sense, elliptic-curve conductor, is not used here). No repo files were modified (read-only respected); the only writes were to the scratchpad.
